positions.name: FlatTechnicalLogbook
positions.frame: How does instrument calibration state get reported as flat technical record without performing for an audience?
positions.why: All three expressions share a single directional read: the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration at 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates, is delivered in native technical jargon with labelled-field structure and no accessibility concession or audience address. The register is flat instrumental record-keeping across the narrative assertion (src-1) and the two metadata fields (src-2, src-3); the temporal stance is uniformly present-realis-concrete; conviction holds at claim level throughout. The shared question is how this instrument-state report performs technical precision as logbook rather than as persuasion or announcement.
